titulo: Irregular pretérito indefinido: Fui, di, vi, hice

aula.objetivo: Use the most frequent irregular verbs in the pretérito indefinido: «ser» and «ir» (fui), «dar», «ver», «hacer», the new-stem verbs («tuve, estuve, pude, puse, supe, quise, vine»), «decir» and «traer» (dijeron, trajeron), and verbs like «pedir» and «dormir» (pidió, durmió).

blocos.titulo: Ser, ir, dar, ver, and hacer in the indefinido
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: a few very common verbs don't follow lesson 19's pattern. They have their own forms, and it's worth memorizing them as whole words. STEP 2: «ser» and «ir» share exactly the same form in the indefinido: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. The meaning comes from the rest of the sentence: «Fui a Madrid» (I went to Madrid, verb «ir») and «Fue un día largo» (it was a long day, verb «ser»). STEP 3: with «ir», the place follows «a»: «Fuimos a la playa», «Fui al médico» (a + el = al). Never with «en». STEP 4: «dar» and «ver» use the same -er/-ir endings but carry no written accent, because they're one-syllable words: di, diste, dio, dimos, disteis, dieron; vi, viste, vio, vimos, visteis, vieron. STEP 5: «hacer» swaps its stem for «hic-»; in the third person singular, the «c» becomes «z» to keep the sound: hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron. STEP 6: none of these forms carries a written accent: «fui», «fue», «di», «vi», «dio», «vio». Writing «fuí» or «vió» is a common mistake. STEP 7: in Latin America, these forms are the same. What changes is frequency: there, «Hoy fui al médico» sounds natural, while Spain tends to prefer «Hoy he ido al médico».
blocos.comparacao: English «went» covers both «ir» and, loosely, a sense of «was» in some idioms, but Spanish folding «ser» and «ir» into the exact same form (fui, fue, fuimos…) has no real English parallel — you have to rely entirely on context to tell them apart, the same way context (not form) tells «I was» from «I went» apart in English, just through different words rather than the same one. The spelling trap here is specific to Spanish: these one-syllable forms (fui, fue, di, vi, dio, vio) never carry a written accent, unlike the two-syllable-or-more regular endings from lesson 19 (hablé, habló) which do.

exemplos.ru: El domingo vi una película con mi primo.
exemplos.pt: On Sunday I watched a movie with my cousin.

exemplos.ru: Mi madre me dio un regalo.
exemplos.pt: My mother gave me a gift.
What did you all do on Friday?

erros.motivo: «Fui» has one syllable and carries no written accent.
In the third person, the «c» becomes «z»: «hizo».
«Vio» has one syllable and carries no accent.

blocos.enunciado: Say six sentences about a recent outing: where you went («Fui a…»), what you saw («Vi…»), what you did («Hice…»), what a friend gave you («Me dio…»), who you went with («Fui con…»), and how it went («Fue…»).
Conjugate «comer» and «escribir» in the indefinido. Then say three sentences about yesterday: one with «ayer», one with «anoche», and one with «hace dos días».
